stories.headline: In-game art flagging reaches draft review, promising coordinate-stamped field notes
stories.summary: Draft PR #111 proposes an opt-in I-key Art Inspector that records local screenshots and world coordinates, plus a read-only collector grouping missing-art flags. It is not merged, validated in Godot, or enabled in production.
stories.body: PR #111 introduces a proposed Art Field Notes workflow for recording missing art during gameplay. An opt-in I-key capture would save local PNG/JSON evidence with world coordinates and bounded visible actors; a Python collector groups flags by spatial stretch. Manifest instructions describe a human-approved, incremental installation lane. The PR is draft and explicitly requests Godot import and runtime smoke tests, privacy/security review and regression validation. It does not generate, approve or install art. Release-mode inspection currently requires broader DevMode flags, so a dedicated inspection-only gate is a material pre-release question. No passing CI or independent review was established. Main remains eef8a41f8e82fe47c346002087f52492d945322a.

article.lead: A practical bridge between spotting missing artwork and fixing it has reached draft review. Art Field Notes would let a developer press I while playing CUSTODIAN, capture where the problem occurs, and later group nearby observations into manageable installation stretches.

sections.heading: From visual annoyance to actionable coordinates
sections.text: The proposed inspector records a local screenshot and JSON with world coordinates and a bounded view of nearby actors. A separate read-only collector groups flags by location so artwork can be matched to the correct manifest entry rather than guessed from memory.

sections.heading: Art approval stays deliberately separate
sections.text: The manifest adds a staged installation workflow, but neither the inspector nor collector approves images or alters gameplay art. A human-approved source and a separately reviewed Asset V2 integration are still required.

sections.heading: The draft has a meaningful release-mode caveat
sections.text: The PR has not passed its requested Godot gameplay smoke tests or security review. Its release-mode opt-in currently uses broader developer flags, so a dedicated inspection-only gate should be considered before wider use.

insights.title: The missing-art backlog could become spatially actionable
insights.explanation: Coordinate-stamped observations would give the art pipeline exact places to repair, connecting playtesting directly to incremental asset installation without automating aesthetic approval.

insights.title: Developer-mode isolation is the key safety gate
insights.explanation: The proposed release opt-in also enables other DevMode features. Separating the inspector's permissions would reduce accidental exposure of unrelated debug capabilities.

article.takeaway: A reviewable implementation candidate now exists, but no gameplay-tested or production-enabled art inspection feature has been established.
article.next_watch: Watch for Godot capture smoke tests, local evidence privacy review, dedicated release gating and an independent acceptance decision.

stories.headline: New art orchestration guide separates candidate production from game-ready approval
stories.summary: CUSTODIAN main now documents a controller-led artwork candidate workflow, including independent screening, verified Dropbox staging, retry limits and restart-safe receipts. This is an operating guide, not proof that the controller ran or any new artwork passed.
stories.body: The November 3 main commit adds ART_CANDIDATE_ORCHESTRATOR_GUIDE.md and routes explicitly authorized Hub/Sepulcher/Awakening candidate work through it. Codex selects assets from the authoritative manifest, asks ChatGPT to generate and screen them, checks actual image bytes and stages passing candidates separately from production. Failed geometry is deferred, not silently accepted. The guide prescribes persistent receipts and recovery, but the commit changes documentation only. No new candidate, independent acceptance, runtime integration or host execution is established. CI status endpoint returned no checks; CI health unknown.

article.lead: The Sepulcher artwork effort now has a written operating playbook for moving from prompts to verified image candidates. It assigns asset selection and recovery to a controller rather than letting the image-generation conversation decide what happens next.

sections.heading: A controlled path from image to candidate
sections.text: The new guide requires the controller to select the next eligible required asset, check generated image dimensions and transparency from actual bytes, obtain a reasoned visual screen, and verify candidate-only Dropbox staging. Failures become explicit deferred obligations.

sections.heading: The approval boundary remains intact
sections.text: A passing candidate is not automatically game-ready artwork. Human aesthetic approval, Asset Pipeline V2 ingestion, runtime registration and scene cutover remain separate gates. The guide also specifies durable receipts and restart reconciliation to avoid accidental regeneration.

sections.heading: A guide is not a running service
sections.text: The inspected commit adds documentation and a root instruction link, not an executing controller or completed image. No fresh host receipt, independent acceptance or production integration was established.

insights.title: The bottleneck is now observable in principle
insights.explanation: Candidate screening, transfer and human approval are explicitly different states. That separation should make failures such as CAL-02 easier to diagnose without counting unfinished art as complete.

insights.title: Recovery is designed before scale-up
insights.explanation: The guide calls for persistent action journals and verification of prior uploads, reducing the risk of duplicate generations after interruptions. Its effectiveness still needs execution evidence.

article.takeaway: The candidate-production procedure has landed on main; operational execution and production art approval have not.
article.next_watch: Watch for an authorized controller run with verifiable image bytes, candidate-screening receipts and a confirmed staged object.

stories.headline: Sepulcher arcade artwork deferred after three failed screens; CAL-03 becomes next candidate
stories.summary: The CAL-02 root-choked arcade failed all three recorded candidate screenings. Its source remains unapproved and unstaged, with further retries unauthorized. The artwork queue can move to independent CAL-03 work without treating CAL-02 as complete.
stories.body: Main now records CAL-02 as DEFERRED_REQUIRED after three failed candidate screens. The last image did not meet the 384×576 native source size, D6 alpha boundary, strict overhead projection, 32px registration or non-room-like silhouette. These are reported screening findings recorded in the manifest, not independently authenticated image bytes. CAL-01 remains the sole staged candidate among 198 required sources; none of the 198 has documented human production approval in this manifest. CAL-03 is next for independent candidate work. CAL-02 needs technical correction and explicit user permission before any retry. This is a manifest disposition, not a runtime asset release.

article.lead: The Sepulcher's root-choked arcade has hit a visual-production gate. Three candidate attempts failed its geometry and presentation rules, so CUSTODIAN has formally deferred the artwork rather than quietly advancing an unsuitable image into the game.

sections.heading: Why the arcade did not pass
sections.text: The recorded screening found a source at 1024×1536 instead of the required 384×576, along with visible pixels outside the D6 footprint, an angled architectural view, inconsistent 32-pixel alignment and a central form that resembled an enterable room. The locked design calls for a strictly overhead, nonwalkable architectural feature.

sections.heading: The queue can move without erasing the debt
sections.text: CAL-02 is now DEFERRED_REQUIRED, not approved or completed. The next independent set is CAL-03. CAL-01 remains the only staged candidate in the 198-source required inventory, and staging is still separate from human approval and game integration.

sections.heading: A retry needs a different approach
sections.text: The artwork maintainer must resolve source sizing, transparent clipping, overhead geometry and grid registration. The three-attempt limit is exhausted, and another CAL-02 generation requires explicit user authorization.

insights.title: A failed image can still improve the production system
insights.explanation: The new disposition makes the failure measurable and preserves the obligation to revisit it, while allowing unrelated art to advance.

insights.title: The failure is geometric, not merely stylistic
insights.explanation: The source conflicts with map footprint and nonwalkable-space constraints. Accepting it would risk depicting navigation that gameplay does not support.

It maps proposed artwork across grounds, shorelines, landmarks and interiors, and adds drift validation. CAL-01 remains a candidate-only paving reference; CAL-02 is next for candidate screening. No human production source approval, Asset V2 registration or gameplay cutover follows from the roadmap. stories.headline: Alpine cliff bunker gains a room-by-room design, but its entrance is not playable yet
stories.summary: A new locked design maps a reversible cliff-bunker entrance, antechamber and later service rooms. Its 26 planned art states span five proposed families, but geometry, source approvals, registration and runtime work remain pending.
stories.body: CUSTODIAN has committed a design and production plan for an enterable Alpine cliff bunker. The plan separates walkable ground, scenic walls, architecture, doors and dressing so the Operator can enter and exit a real space rather than a painted cutaway. The 26-state inventory is planning only: 14 initial, nine later and three optional. Two inspected transparent image references are composition guides, not approved production art. No room geometry, Asset V2 registration, runtime binding, independent review or playable entrance is established by this commit. The next gate is a no-art real-Operator blockout to establish reversible ingress, collision, floor masks and door anchors before producing final assets.

article.lead: The Alpine cliff bunker now has a concrete plan for becoming somewhere the Operator can actually enter. The new design replaces the temptation to treat a dramatic cutaway as a playable room with a sequence of physical spaces, starting at the snowy approach and antechamber.

sections.heading: From scenery to a traversable place
sections.text: The design calls for reversible ingress, a physical threshold and antechamber, then service and control rooms in a later stage. Walkable floors and collision must be established independently of decorative scenery. That distinction matters because a beautiful cliff illustration alone cannot tell the game where a character may stand or pass.

sections.heading: The art inventory is mapped, not delivered
sections.text: The manifest names 26 states across five proposed asset families: 14 for the initial pass, nine for expansion and three optional. Two transparent 1254-pixel references were inspected as composition guides, but are not approved source assets. Exact floor masks, room canvases and door anchors are still pending.

insights.title: A manifest is not an asset shipment

stories.headline: CUSTODIAN clarifies ownership of original game material while preserving earlier MIT grants
stories.summary: A new main-branch licensing update marks original CUSTODIAN material proprietary and archives two historical MIT notices verbatim. The change explicitly preserves valid earlier permissions and third-party licenses; it does not resolve provenance of every asset or alter gameplay.
stories.body: The project now has a repository-wide proprietary notice for original materials owned by its named rights holder. Two MIT notices previously in the Godot project tree are retained verbatim in licensing history. The new text explicitly says prior valid permissions are not retroactively withdrawn and separately owned components keep their own terms. This is a documentation and distribution-policy milestone, not evidence of a game build, a legal determination of asset ownership, or a change to runtime behavior. Historical names ShardSpace and [Lighar] still require provenance verification before any specific files can be confidently assigned.
bullets: Repository-wide proprietary notice added for owned original materials.
Both prior MIT notices retained verbatim in licensing history.
Earlier valid grants and third-party licenses expressly preserved.
Asset-by-asset provenance remains an open distribution gate.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN has clarified how its original game material is licensed, without attempting to erase the project's earlier open-source history. The new notice protects original work prospectively while preserving the permissions and third-party obligations that already exist.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: The main branch now carries a proprietary notice for original code, artwork, writing and other materials owned by the named rights holder. Two older MIT notices have been copied verbatim into a historical record rather than silently discarded.

sections.heading: What the notice cannot settle
sections.text: The text expressly preserves valid permissions previously granted and licenses belonging to outside contributors or incorporated components. It also acknowledges that the identities attached to the historical notices do not establish ownership of individual files.

insights.title: Distribution needs a provenance map
insights.explanation: A clear current policy is useful, but the license file alone cannot establish who owns every imported asset or code component. A file-level provenance check remains important before distributing the game.

insights.title: Historical grants remain a separate obligation
insights.explanation: The preserved MIT notices prevent the current policy from being mistaken for a retroactive withdrawal of valid older rights.

article.takeaway: The licensing documentation has changed on main; ownership provenance and third-party compliance still require independent review before distribution.
article.next_watch: A component-level attribution and provenance audit, especially for materials associated with the historical notices.

stories.headline: Sepulcher Gardens art plan shifts to modular paving, preserving the playable map
stories.summary: A new main-branch correction replaces the proposed rectangular Gardens ground painting with one 512×512 repeatable floor-material candidate. The existing irregular walkability mask remains authoritative. Earlier paving is explicitly unapproved, and the separate architecture layer remains blocked pending a footprint contract.
stories.body: CUSTODIAN's Sepulcher Gardens art guidance now calls for a 512×512 seamless opaque ground-material candidate, repeated and clipped to the existing irregular walkability mask rather than painted as an entire rectangular room. This prevents an art plate from silently redefining traversable terrain. Existing paving candidates are unapproved references, including one reported to fail a 3×3 tiling check. CAL-01 is still awaiting generation and individual human approval; CAL-02 structural presentation remains blocked on an approved footprint contract. This commit changes source-art instructions and manifest metadata, not the game renderer or an accepted asset.

insights.title: The next milestone is still a candidate

stories.headline: Empty Convoy fails its post-fix gameplay sign-off despite passing focused tests
stories.summary: A post-land manual check did not accept the Empty Convoy encounter correction. The Operator reached the prepared approach point, but the reviewer reported a possible scenario mismatch; the exact cause remains unknown. A separate documented QA checkout was safely retired, with host-reported disk recovery. Independent review remains outstanding.
stories.body: The security correction was previously landed and passed targeted headless tests. The subsequent authorized GUI check reached its prepared approach, but the human reviewer returned NOT_ACCEPTED and reported a possible encounter mismatch. No successful defense, custody trace or exactly-once salvage was confirmed. The post-land closeout receipt reports scoped evidence preservation and non-forced removal of one detached QA worktree, with disk free increasing by about 6.92 GiB. These are documented host observations, not independently remeasured by WIRE. The original gameplay failure is unresolved; no paired review PASS is established. Main also contains a subsequent whitespace-only receipt edit.

article.lead: Empty Convoy's security correction has met its first significant post-land obstacle: the human gameplay check did not accept it. The Operator reached the prepared encounter approach, but the reviewer still could not confirm that the intended scenario behaved correctly. Passing focused tests has not yet translated into a successful player-facing encounter.

sections.heading: The test reached the site, not the finish line
sections.text: The documented GUI run positioned the Operator for a manual check. The reviewer returned a possible scenario or encounter mismatch. No confirmed defender battle, custody trace or one-time salvage result followed, leaving the original failure unexplained.

sections.heading: Cleanup succeeded on a narrower evidentiary footing
sections.text: The closeout record describes preservation of QA evidence, scoped cleanup and ordinary removal of a detached checkout. It reports one fewer attached worktree and about 6.92 GiB more free disk. WIRE has not independently inspected the host, so these are source-reported measurements, not live telemetry.

insights.title: A passing security test can miss a scenario mismatch
insights.explanation: The correction guards against treating failed enemy spawns as victory, but the manual outcome suggests the remaining problem may involve reaching or identifying the intended encounter. That possibility needs diagnosis, not an assumed fix.

insights.title: A closed QA checkout does not close the gameplay issue
insights.explanation: The temporary test environment can be retired while the correction remains unaccepted. Cleanup and gameplay acceptance are distinct gates.

article.takeaway: The fix is landed and test-backed, but the player-facing Empty Convoy outcome is not accepted; the root cause remains unconfirmed.
article.next_watch: A source-bound diagnosis of the manual scenario mismatch, a fresh integrated retest and a separate independent review disposition.
